name: Cross-sectional funding dispersion — long the most-negative-funding names (long, 4h)
rationale: MECHANISM: funding compression hit BTC/ETH hardest (quant-saturated), but mid-cap/long-tail perps keep 2-5x the APR because liquidity is thin and funding is STICKY — fewer arbitrageurs bother. Across the universe each 4h bar, the most-NEGATIVE-funding names (crowded shorts = squeeze fuel) tend to out-perform: they pay a spot long carry (funding_feature) AND recover as shorts cover. We take the long leg only (direction +1, spot-only live constraint), entering names whose funding_rate is deeply negative (bottom of the cross-section) and filtering by a minimum open_interest so the name is tradable. The other side is retail chasing leverage in illiquid alts; a systematic solo farms the dispersion the giants avoid (too small for their size). DISCONFIRMER 1: kill if the edge is an illusion once REAL fees + slippage on thin books are charged (0.06% taker on wide-spread alts eats the funding spread) — the classic long-tail trap. DISCONFIRMER 2: kill if the return is disguised beta/size (most-negative-funding = most-beaten-down alts = high-beta bounce) and dies after neutralizing to trailing return. DISCONFIRMER 3: kill if too few tradable perps have reliable funding+OI history (breadth too low for effective-N).
catalyst: the deepest-negative-funding names in the cross-section, filtered for tradable OI — a sticky-funding long tilt.
